title: Recursion
summary: Solve a small problem by calling the same function on a smaller one. Follow the stop rule and returning answers in six languages.
introduction: Imagine four small boxes inside one another. You open a box until you reach the empty one, then close them in reverse order. Recursion follows a similar path: a function asks a smaller version of itself for help, then finishes its own job.
learningObjectives: Write a base case that stops repeated calls
Trace how waiting calls combine their answers

blocks.text: Recursion means a function calls itself. Each call has its own input. To find 1 + 2 + 3 + 4, we can add 4 to the smaller answer 1 + 2 + 3.
The base case is an answer small enough to give immediately. Here the sum up to 0 is 0. The recursive step reduces n by 1 so every allowed input eventually reaches that stop rule.
The call stack is the computer's list of waiting function calls. When the smallest call returns, the computer resumes the most recent waiting call first.

items: sumTo(4) waits for sumTo(3), then will add 4.
sumTo(3) waits for sumTo(2), and sumTo(2) waits for sumTo(1). Each waits to add its own number.
sumTo(1) asks for sumTo(0). The base case returns 0 immediately.

blocks.text: The same program in six languages

Choose the language you are learning. Each tab solves the same problem and prints the same result. JavaScript can run in this page. The other tabs need separate local tools: a C11 compiler, a C++17 compiler, Python 3, .NET 8 or later for C#, or Java 17. Use Program.cs for C# and Main.java for Java.
The first line is 10, the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + 4. The second call starts at the base case and prints 0 without calling itself again.
This teaching function expects a small non-negative whole number. Try values from 0 to 20. A negative number keeps getting smaller and never reaches 0. A fraction is outside the contract too.

Even valid large numbers can make too many waiting calls or exceed the size of an integer. A loop would use less stack room for this simple sum. Recursion is useful when a problem naturally breaks into smaller pieces, such as trees.
How much work and extra room?
For input n, the function makes n + 1 calls, including the call at 0. Each call does a small fixed amount of work, so time is O(n).
At the deepest point, about n calls are waiting. They use O(n) extra stack space. Returning answers does not erase the space that was needed at that deepest moment.

blocks.title: Try one small change
blocks.text: Change sumTo(4) to sumTo(3). Write the returns 0, 1, 3, and 6 on paper. The first printed result should become 6.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: A base case alone is not enough. The next call must move toward it. Calling sumTo(n) again, or adding 1 here, never reaches the base case for a positive input.
